features.name: Academic Credential Level
features.description: Captures the strength or level of the applicant's relevant formal technical education.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic Systems Design
features.description: Captures hands-on design ownership of agent-based systems with explicit control boundaries, supervision, guardrails, or supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic-systems experience is mentioned.
Agents are mentioned only vaguely, with little indication of direct design or implementation.
The letter shows clear experience building or working on agentic tooling, but with limited architectural detail.
The letter shows end-to-end design of Python agents paired with Go services, backends, or guardrails.
The letter shows especially mature agentic design, emphasizing constraints, permissions, auditability, or strategic infrastructure direction.

features.name: Algorithmic Fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering problem-solving.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms.
Gives a specific example of choosing a better structure or redesigning logic algorithmically.
Gives a strong example showing substantial performance, scalability, or tractability improvement from algorithmic skill.

features.name: Applied AI Production Maturity
features.description: Captures real production experience deploying AI or LLM systems with attention to reliability, evaluation, hardening, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Developer Enablement Mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as helping engineers take the safe path through better defaults, lower friction, and user-centered workflows.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering Rigor
features.description: Captures the stated quality bar of correctness, reliability, careful boundaries, and disciplined engineering for security-sensitive work.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives little signal about quality, testing, reliability, or maintainability.
The letter gestures at seriousness or standards, but without concrete habits or practices.
The letter clearly emphasizes dependable systems, testing, maintainability, guardrails, or careful design.
The letter strongly signals security-critical rigor, with explicit habits such as typed or tested tooling, auditable boundaries, reliability-first design, or builder-quality standards.

features.name: Evidence Specificity
features.description: Captures whether claims are backed by concrete examples, mechanisms, technical detail, or quantified support rather than broad assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go Depth
features.description: Captures how central and substantial Go is in the applicant's recent production engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact Articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the outcomes or practical effects of the applicant's work rather than only listing responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists interests or responsibilities with no clear outcomes.
Provides background counts but little evidence of what changed because of the work.
Shows at least one clear result or before-and-after effect.
Shows concrete, vivid, or measured outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to evaluate.

features.name: Learning and Collaboration Posture
features.description: Captures openness to learning from specialists and collaborating humbly to deepen security expertise.

levels.descriptor: Shows no sign of wanting to grow through security collaboration.
Shows indirect openness to learning or collaboration.
Explicitly emphasizes learning from security engineers or deepening security craft on the job.

features.name: Maintainer Mindset
features.description: Captures emphasis on long-term operability, maintainability, failure handling, and stewardship of inherited or long-lived systems.

levels.descriptor: Does not signal any particular maintenance or operability orientation.
Briefly references reliability, testing, or keeping systems running.
Clearly emphasizes maintenance, inherited systems, or the responsibility of operating durable services.
Expresses a strong stewardship ethos, such as building for inheritance, quiet resilience, higher standards, or long-term operational trust.

features.name: Narrative Cohesion
features.description: Captures how smoothly the letter forms a coherent, well-structured case rather than a disconnected list of points.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative Distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable, individual, and non-template the letter's voice or framing feels.

levels.descriptor: The letter feels interchangeable, checklist-driven, or heavily templated.
The letter has some personal framing, but is still mostly standard and forgettable.
The letter has a noticeable voice or framing device that helps the applicant stand out.
The letter delivers a vivid, controlled narrative that is both memorable and well matched to the role.

features.name: Offensive Security Practice
features.description: Captures ongoing hands-on adversarial practice outside routine development work, especially CTF-style participation.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-Source Stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public or upstream code through contribution, maintenance, releases, upstream fixes, or community and user ownership.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Personal Project Ambition
features.description: Captures the technical depth, seriousness, and role-relevant ambition of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform Leverage Orientation
features.description: Captures motivation toward foundational or central infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or systems.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production Experience
features.description: Captures the amount and maturity of directly relevant professional production-software experience, often signaled by years worked and sustained operational ownership.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of clearly relevant experience, or tenure is not stated.
About 2 to 3 years of relevant experience; clears the minimum but is still early-career for this role.
About 4 to 5 years of relevant experience; solid mid-level tenure.
6 or more years of relevant experience; deep tenure for this opening.

features.name: Production Service Scope
features.description: Captures the breadth of hands-on exposure to distinct production services and launch or maintenance cycles.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Python Depth
features.description: Captures how substantial and production-ready the applicant's Python experience appears for services, tooling, or automation.

levels.descriptor: Python is not mentioned.
Python is mentioned, but only as a general tool or scripting language.
Python is clearly used regularly for services, tooling, or automation.
Python is presented as production-grade work, with specifics such as typed or tested services, shared tooling, or major automation ownership.

features.name: Role-Specific Motivation and Fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter connects the applicant's motivation and background to this exact role and its stated responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security Assessment Practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience evaluating systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, and fix validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security Automation Framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role or team as scaling scarce security expertise through automation, triage systems, agentic workflows, or similar leverage.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security Credential Strength
features.description: Captures the strength or rigor of formal external security certifications or credentials cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security Engineering Philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful worldview about what security engineering is for and how secure systems should be approached.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinctive security philosophy beyond generic enthusiasm.
Shows broad positive sentiment about security or impact, but little deeper framing.
Expresses a clear philosophy about rigor, resilience, secure defaults, or invisible success.
Offers a memorable, specific philosophy that strongly reinforces fit for this kind of security work.

features.name: Vulnerability Triage Automation
features.description: Captures direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability or security-finding intake, triage, routing, deduplication, or prioritization.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing Polish
features.description: Captures freedom from distracting spelling, grammar, proofreading, and other surface-level errors.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures genuinely distinct leftover constructs that do not clearly share a recurring underlying dimension with other entries.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
